pool.text: David Thompson wintered with Piikani Nation along the Bow River.
John Glenn became first documented European settler in Calgary area.
Three priests built a log cabin on the Elbow River banks.
Site became a North-West Mounted Police post.
Fort Calgary officially established after minister's approval.
First Nations ceded title to Fort Calgary region via Treaty 7.
R.B. Bennett's Conservative Party wins federal election, becomes prime minister.
Pat Lenihan elected to Calgary City Council via proportional representation.
Premier William Aberhart moves to Calgary for provincial election.
Opening of the Southern Alberta Jubilee Auditorium.
University of Calgary gains degree‑granting autonomy.
Rise of Peter Lougheed's Progressive Conservative Party due to oil sector.
Council directs design and construction of CTrain south leg.
Nelson Skalbania announces relocation of Atlanta Flames to Calgary.
CTrain south leg begins operation on May 25.
City Council announces service cuts amid $16 million deficit.
Completion of Petro‑Canada Centre marks end of construction boom.
Co‑hosting of World Junior Ice Hockey Championships with Edmonton and Red Deer.
Canadian Pacific Railway moved headquarters from Montreal to Calgary.
Imperial Oil relocated its headquarters to Calgary.
